{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABco7qww", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhGLH9I", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 130, "title": "Preinstall a bootable FreeDOS(98) IDE HDD in the PC-9821Ap browser demo and separate floppy insertion from boot selection", "body": "## Problem

The browser demo now defaults to **PC-9821Ap DOS + Auto media insertion** ([Issue #120](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/issues/120), [PR #121](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/pull/121)), but starts with **no disk in any drive**. A newcomer who inserts a **data-only DOS game D88** can encounter `NO SYSTEM` because its floppy is not bootable. The user wants the browser to feel like a ready-to-use PC-9821: **a reasonably sized IDE hard disk with FreeDOS(98) already installed and booting automatically**, while floppy drives are initially empty and available for games and data disks. Users should not first have to find/build a DOS boot floppy.

**Current behavior to correct:** `web/app.js` starts with `mounted = [null, null, null]` and no built-in HDD preload. `Machine::insert` in `src/lib.rs` currently selects floppy boot when inserting drive 0 and HDD boot when inserting drive 2. The browser's Auto router sends D88/HDM/etc. to FDD1, which both mounts it and immediately resets/boots. With a preinstalled DOS HDD, **inserting a floppy must not automatically replace the preferred HDD boot source** or reboot the running DOS session. Inserting into FDD2 already supports live access, thanks to [Issue #126 / PR #128](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/pull/128); do not regress that.

## Expected outcome

A **fresh visit** to the public browser demo selects **PC-9821Ap DOS** and automatically has an installed, **bootable, writable FreeDOS(98) IDE HDD**. It boots to a real, responsive DOS prompt **without the user uploading any media, pressing a demo button or possessing a proprietary BIOS/ROM**.

- Target **128 MiB logical HDI capacity** as the sensible starting size suggested in the discussion (FAT16 is likely appropriate), with practical free space for future DOS file copies. The *actual network transfer* must be **small and measured**; **do not make visitors download a raw 128 MiB disk** merely to obtain a tiny DOS system. Use a reproducible compact/compressed/sparse template or similarly simple efficient mechanism, locally expanding into the established HDI geometry and disk representation as needed. Measure page-start download, startup time and memory; choose the smallest coherent implementation that meets real browser limits.
- The HDD must boot **actual GPL FreeDOS(98) kernel + FreeCOM guest code**, with an original/MIT boot/partition helper as necessary, using the already pinned lawful inputs; no JavaScript-implemented DOS, synthetic prompt, hardcoded guest success, commercial content, NEC ROM/font dumps or borrowed emulator core.
- **FDD1/FDD2 start empty.** On normal use, inserting or dragging a supported floppy (.d88/.d98/.hdm/.tfd/.xdf/.2hd/.img) **mounts media for the running DOS** without rebooting it or replacing the selected HDD boot source. The user can see and access the floppy through the guest DOS, including hot insertion, swap/eject and keyboard commands. Do not assume the DOS drive letter if guest enumeration differs.
- Offer a clear, minimal **explicit boot-source choice** (HDD as the default, Floppy 1 when requested), with predictable **Reset/Boot** behavior. This choice is separate from **Auto / Floppy 1 / Floppy 2 / IDE HDD insertion destination**; selecting a drive to *insert* media never silently changes boot preference. Booting a floppy should remain available for standalone game disks; do not prevent users from running the built-in Star Trail or Hello world + BEEP demos. Switching back to the default HDD should not require a page reload.
- Preserve manual media controls. A user-supplied HDI should be able to **replace** the bundled default HDD intentionally, not silently be mixed with it; show clear source/filename/active boot status and avoid data loss when replacing a modified HDD. Eject/Export/Reset must target the correct media, and exporting the built-in HDD should include all guest writes. Retain local-only in-memory changes until export; **no implicit durable browser storage or upload**.
- **PC-9801VM** remains manually selectable with its documented limitations, without crashing or trying to boot the PC-9821-only IDE disk. Switching profiles and returning to Ap has explicit, consistent behavior for the default/custom HDD and floppy state. Keep the Rust library/headless profile default contract unless there is a demonstrated reason to change it; browser startup alone changes.

## Context and implementation pointers

- [`web/index.html`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/web/index.html): PC-9821Ap/Auto already selected, initially `No disk`; current UI has a `Reset boots` status line.
- [`web/app.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/web/app.js): `mounted`, `lastDrive`, `resolveDrive`, `loadBytes`, built-in demo handlers, asynchronous chunked HDI import/export, profile switch and reset. Startup loads `core.wasm` but currently no guest HDD. Prevent startup races with user input, profile changes and large-media import; show meaningful loading/errors and allow retry/recovery.
- [`src/lib.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/src/lib.rs) and [`src/firmware.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/src/firmware.rs): boot preference and guest BIOS HDD/FDD selection. Introduce the **smallest explicit boot-source operation** needed to decouple insertion from boot, retaining headless/native compatibility and correct firmware semantics. Avoid creating a second competing boot policy in JS.
- [`tools/prepare_freedos.py`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/tools/prepare_freedos.py) and [`tools/prepare_freedos_hdd_fixture.py`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/tools/prepare_freedos_hdd_fixture.py): pinned GPL DOS kernel/FreeCOM, complete corresponding sources/notices and original MIT partition boot helpers. The existing 4 MiB `fixtures/freedos/shell.hdi` is **test-only**, not currently published; its 4 MiB FAT12 geometry is not itself the desired larger desktop. Reuse its lawful guest provenance and real boot path, but generate a suitable desktop disk with a deterministic, independently auditable FAT layout.
- [`docs/large-hdi.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/large-hdi.md) and [PR #129](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/pull/129): supports large HDI and bounded/chunked browser I/O, with real guest FAT16 testing beyond 128 MiB. Do **not** undo large-drive behavior or add a duplicate full 128 MiB JS transfer buffer.
- [`docs/floppy-hot-insert-validation.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/floppy-hot-insert-validation.md): guest DOS live FDD2 handling, DOS drive enumeration and refresh on media swaps.
- [`docs/licenses.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/licenses.md) and [build/site asset audit](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/README.md#reproduce-the-checks): existing browser release currently has a strict 10-asset allowlist. A publicly delivered FreeDOS guest is **a change in licensed publication scope**, not just another test fixture.

### License and publication requirements (mandatory)

FreeDOS(98)/FreeCOM and boot components must be **lawfully redistributable** in this specific assembled boot disk. Pin the **exact binary/source/license provenance and checksums** for all guest components. Deliver complete corresponding GPL source code and notices under applicable terms **through durable, accessible download links or packaged source archives** at the published site, with clear links from `web/licenses.html` / README; ensure the selected GPL version's requirements are met, without incorrectly assuming that an upstream link alone always satisfies source obligations. Preserve required copyright notices and conditions. Update the **explicit public-asset allowlist/audit** to allow only intentional new guest disk/template/license/source artifacts. Do not accidentally publish other generated `fixtures/freedos` disks, upstream utilities/slack, original protected fonts/BIOS or private/copyright-restricted game/media assets.

Keep independently generated/legal media and any large intermediate raw HDI outside version control and Pages unless the deliberately published, rights-cleared distributable is explicitly audited. Reproducible preparation should validate the source hashes, FAT partition/header/geometry and resulting guest contents. Preserve the project's original Rust-only emulator restriction; GPL guest code executes as guest software and is not linked into or translated into the emulator.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Boot on fresh visit:** Production Rust/Wasm demo selects Ap and boots the installed, properly formatted **~128 MiB logical IDE HDD** with genuine FreeDOS(98)/FreeCOM to an **interactive DOS prompt**, without user action, from both `/` and `/pc98-rust/`. Assert actual guest kernel handoff, DOS commands/keyboard response and repeated boot on Reset, rather than checking only a startup message or UI `Running`.
- [ ] **Efficient delivery:** Provide a deterministic compact/sparse/compressed built-in HDI construction path, measure actual **network asset size, browser peak/steady memory, boot time** and compare with a full 128 MiB transfer. Avoid any unnecessary full-size intermediate copy in JS and excessive startup delay. Correctly handle build/source failures, fetch errors, partial assembly, size/geometry mismatch, out-of-memory and user/profile changes while loading. The existing local large-HDI import/export remains functional.
- [ ] **Independent boot selection:** A separate, clearly visible and accessible choice of **Boot from HDD (default)** or **Boot from Floppy 1** controls next Reset. Inserting an ordinary floppy in Auto or manual FDD1/FDD2 does not reboot DOS or change HDD boot preference. Selecting an insertion destination is not itself a boot request. A deliberate explicit floppy boot restarts/boots genuine floppy IPL and can be switched back to HDD. Preserve deterministic fallback/error behavior if the chosen medium is absent; no silent switches to some other disk.
- [ ] **DOS live floppy workflow:** From an already running default HDD DOS shell, mount a legal independent original FAT/D88 data disk in FDD1 and FDD2 as appropriate, use genuine guest DOS to discover/execute `DIR`/`TYPE` or an original test COM, then swap/eject and reaccess media without resetting. Assert real guest FDC activity and unchanged/write-protected disk invariants. Do not assume `B:` when an HDD is present; follow actual DOS drive assignments. If specific HDD-booted DOS FDD cache/drive-letter behavior needs a new fix, address it with independent tests.
- [ ] **Media lifecycle:** Preserve existing media routing and manual override, reset, eject, export/save including guest writes, and explicit user HDI replacement. Never overwrite a dirty built-in or user HDD without a clear destructive-action warning and choice to cancel/export. Report clear media names and selected boot device. A new visit defaults to the clean installed HDD; no server save, implicit persistence or uploads. Treat export-to-file and reimport as the persistence route.
- [ ] **Profiles and demos:** Switching to PC-9801VM never attempts IDE boot; returning to Ap maintains or clearly recreates the intended mounted disk state. Both bundled MIT demos still work on both profiles and can intentionally boot FDD1 even while the built-in HDD is mounted; returning to the FreeDOS HDD remains possible. Retain keyboard/mouse/audio and full-sized user HDI behavior.
- [ ] **License/source publication:** Audit every redistributed guest binary, supply complete matching GPL sources and license notices through the published site/links in a legally compliant way, pin hashes and verify generated disks, prevent unrelated DOS utilities/private game/media from being published. Update the explicit approved-assets list and verify what actually ships. A page containing only the binary without necessary source/notice access does **not** satisfy acceptance.
- [ ] **Tests and CI:** Run applicable original and GPL fixture preparations; `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`; release Wasm build; exact site-asset/license/source audit; and the complete **real production-Wasm Chromium suite** on **both `/` and `/pc98-rust/`**, plus cold/reset, floppy hot-swap and deliberate boot override scenarios. Preserve existing guest-owned assertions, browser performance principles, test isolation and large-HDI tests. Do not add private adult games, require manual playtesting, emulate DOS behavior in JavaScript or merely mock the shell.
- [ ] Update README, browser instructions and license page with the **HDD-installed default experience**, the boot-source vs insertion-drive distinction, PC-9801VM behavior, guest drive letters, export/reset/reload semantics and compatibility limits. Align with [UI/UX principles](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/README.md#uiux), avoiding unnecessary controls or extra prose.

Use the standard **Issue → implementation → PR → AI review → merge** flow with all Issue/PR/review/commit text in **English**. The scope is one complete boot-ready desktop experience, not a Windows emulator or general DOS installer. Keep unrelated CPU hardware additions out unless independently demonstrated by a legal guest.

## Optional validation

Local manual desktop/mobile UX check: fresh open -> DOS prompt; Auto D88 mounts as a data floppy without booting it; optionally boot a floppy game; return to HDD; export/reinsert modified built-in HDD. No commercial game, physical PC-98, live deployed site or adult-media test is required to approve the PR.

## Required post-merge verification

None. GitHub Pages and deployment-only checks can be reported after merge; failures should be tracked with a separate `task` Issue, not imposed as pre-merge approval gates.
